brief.outcome: Bring the no-show rate at the five-stylist Manchester salon from 18% of booked appointments to under 8% within two months, without losing regular clients.

ambition.goal_beyond: Full chairs: the slots that stylists hold are filled by clients who turn up, and a slot that does free up is refilled instead of lost
rungs: Add a stronger reminder to Fresha than the single 24-hour message
Find which clients, services, days and lead times drive the no-shows and apply a deposit or card-on-file policy only where it pays, leaving regulars alone
Keep it true: a weekly no-show check by client group that flags a slide early, with a way to refill freed slots
ambition.judge: The Fresha appointments report (completed against no-show, by client group), read against the 18% baseline and the three months before

brief.deliverable: A checked picture of who no-shows and when, a new reminder and confirmation sequence and a fair cancellation policy set up in Fresha by the owner, and a weekly readout of the no-show rate by client group against 8%
done: Fresha appointment history rebuilt and the 18% reproduced from the rows
Reminder delivery and no-show marking checked
Diagnosis with every hypothesis marked supported, refuted or unknown
Owner's choice recorded, including who a deposit or card on file applies to
Reminder messages and policy wording written and checked for fairness and plain language
Settings changed by the owner in steps, with regulars kept out of any fee
Weekly readout of the no-show rate against 8% with guardrails checked
brief.deadline: Two months from the first setting change
guardrails: Regular clients keep booking: their rebooking rate does not fall more than 5% from the baseline
Total booked appointments per week do not fall more than 5% below the baseline
Any fee or deposit is clear before booking, proportionate to the real loss (about 45 pounds a no-show) and never applied to regular clients without the owner's say
Reminder messages carry only booking information, not promotions
limits: No deposits are taken now; any deposit or fee is a decision for the owner
Fresha is reached through the browser and the owner changes the settings herself
Working data stays in a spreadsheet in this project, with client names and phone numbers removed
assets: The owner's own knowledge of her regular clients
brief.data_home: A spreadsheet in this project, as the owner asked; appointment IDs only, no names or phone numbers
brief.technical_level: Comfortable changing Fresha settings herself; wants exact steps and ready wording
unknowns: How many appointments the salon books each month
Which clients, services, days and lead times have the most no-shows
How Fresha counts late cancellations next to no-shows
Whether reminders are delivered to every client (phone numbers present and valid)
How many freed slots are refilled today

answers.question: The business
answers.answer: Hair salon with five stylists in Manchester

answers.question: The problem
answers.answer: No-show rate is 18% of booked appointments over the last three months (Fresha booking report)

answers.question: What exists
answers.answer: Fresha sends one reminder 24 hours before; no deposits now

answers.question: Cost
answers.answer: Each no-show costs about 45 pounds on average

answers.question: Target
answers.answer: No-shows under 8% within two months without losing regular clients

answers.question: Access
answers.answer: Fresha through the browser; the owner can change settings herself

research.approach: Practitioners treat no-shows as a pattern, not a general problem. They export every appointment with its status, split the no-show rate by new or returning client, lead time, day and time, service and stylist, and only then choose rules. Reminders come first because they are cheap and well studied: a systematic review found text reminders cut missed appointments by about a quarter and that several reminders beat one. Deposits or a card on file come second and only where the no-show rate is high, such as new clients or long-lead bookings, because a fee asked of everyone costs regular clients. Fees must be visible before booking and proportionate to the real loss. Everything is introduced in steps with regulars as a built-in comparison group, and read weekly.

sources.title: Using digital notifications to improve attendance in clinic: systematic review and meta-analysis (BMJ Open)
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review: text reminders were linked to about 25% fewer missed appointments (15% against 21%), and multiple notifications worked better than a single one. Health clinics, not salons, so use as direction.

sources.title: Fresha Help: Charge no-show and cancellation fees
sources.note: Vendor documentation: a no-show fee needs a payment policy, taken as a deposit or from a saved card; a no-show can be marked only after the start time until the end of that day; a charged fee cannot be reversed. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Fresha Help: Payments policies overview
sources.note: Vendor documentation: a default payment policy applies to bookings and can be overridden per service; deposits suit high-value services, new clients or peak times; policy terms are shown to clients and reminders can repeat them. Read through a search summary; no date shown; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: CMA: Unfair contract terms explained (CMA37)
sources.note: UK regulator guidance on when standard terms are unfair. The listing page was readable; the cancellation-charge specifics (charges should reflect the real loss and be clear before booking) come from secondary summaries and should be checked in the full guide.

steps.name: Export every appointment with its status and rebuild the 18%
steps.why: 18% is a report until the rows reproduce it, and how late cancellations are counted changes the answer.

steps.name: Check reminders are delivered and no-shows are marked the same way
steps.why: A client with no valid number never gets the reminder, and inconsistent marking hides the pattern.

steps.name: Split no-shows by client type, lead time, day and time, service and stylist
steps.why: The rule should target the groups where no-shows concentrate and leave regulars alone.

steps.name: Add more reminders with a one-tap confirm or reschedule
steps.why: Several reminders beat one, and a confirm step lets the salon release the slot.

steps.name: Set a fair deposit or card-on-file rule for the high-risk groups only
steps.why: A fee protects the slot where risk is high, and must be clear before booking and in line with the real loss.

steps.name: Introduce changes in steps and compare with regulars as the control
steps.why: Steps show which change worked, and unaffected regulars show whether something else changed.

steps.name: Read the no-show rate weekly by group against the baseline
steps.why: Weekly reading shows early whether the rate is moving and whether regulars are being lost.

steps.name: Overbook the diary to cover expected no-shows
steps.why: Some salons double-book slots to cover no-shows.

pitfalls.text: Asking every client for a deposit when no-shows come mostly from new clients or long-lead bookings, and losing regulars.
Counting late cancellations as no-shows, or marking them inconsistently, so the baseline is wrong.
Reminders that go to clients with no valid number, so the rate does not move.
A cancellation fee or deposit that is hidden until after booking or far above the real loss, which UK consumer rules can treat as unfair.
Changing reminders, deposits and wording together, so no change can be credited.
Judging the result in under two months or on too few appointments, so season or luck gets the credit.

plan.name: Cut no-shows with better reminders and a deposit only where it pays

stages.name: Pin down the goal
stages.goal: Turn the request into a measured goal, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Rebuild the appointment history
stages.goal: Load the Fresha appointment history with outcomes into the spreadsheet, with names and numbers replaced by IDs, and reproduce the 18% no-show rate.

checks.name: No-shows divided by booked appointments for the last 3 months is within 1 percentage point of the reported 18%, or the gap is explained
The treatment of late cancellations, same-day cancellations and walk-ins is stated
No client name, phone number or email is in the spreadsheet
Missing fields are named with what each blocks

stages.name: Check reminders and marking can be trusted
stages.goal: Check that reminders reach clients, that no-shows are marked the same way by every stylist and that the data can support group findings.

checks.name: The share of booked appointments where a reminder was sent and delivered is stated
No-show rate is compared across the five stylists and a gap of more than 2 times is explained as marking or real
The rule for when a no-show can be marked is recorded
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the group findings

stages.name: Find who no-shows and when
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses on client type, lead time, day and time, service, stylist, reminders and regulars, and keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers used
A group finding needs at least 30 appointments in the group, otherwise it is marked low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
States what 8% means in no-shows per month and in pounds at 45 each, and how far reminders alone (about a quarter fewer, from the review) could go, or marks the booking volume unknown

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked options (more reminders with confirm, card on file for some groups, deposit for some services, wording, refill list) with expected effect on no-shows, risk to regulars, effort, confidence and measurement.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected effect, effort, confidence, risk to regular clients and how it is measured
Reminders rank before fees unless the diagnosis shows reminders already reach and work
No option applies a fee or deposit to regular clients unless the data shows they no-show above 8%

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks the options and the groups a deposit or card on file applies to. Ask for the reason when the top option is passed over and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are in decisions.jsonl
The groups any fee applies to are named, with the fee amount and the notice period

stages.name: Write the reminders and the policy wording
stages.goal: Write the reminder and confirm messages, the cancellation and deposit wording shown at booking, and a short note to regular clients, ready to paste into Fresha with exact steps.

outputs.name: Messages, policy wording and Fresha steps

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included
Policy wording states the fee, the notice period and what happens with illness in plain words, at a reading level of about grade 8
Reminders carry only booking information and a confirm or reschedule link, with no promotion
Each text message is checked for length, sender and send cost
Each Fresha setting change has click-by-click steps and a way to check it worked, such as a test booking

stages.optional_when: No reminder or policy option was chosen.

stages.name: Change Fresha in steps
stages.goal: The owner changes Fresha settings in two steps: stronger reminders for everyone, then the chosen deposit or card on file for the chosen groups only. Register the comparison before the first change.

checks.name: The comparison is registered in experiments.jsonl before the first change: step dates, groups, the 3-month baseline and regulars as the unaffected group
The two steps are at least 3 weeks apart, so each can be read
A test booking shows the new reminder and, if used, the policy wording as a client sees it
Regular clients are confirmed to be outside any fee, or the owner has approved otherwise

stages.name: Read the no-show rate weekly
stages.goal: Each week read the no-show rate by client group, booked appointments, online booking and regulars' rebooking against the baseline and the guardrails.

checks.name: Rates come from Fresha appointment rows with the same no-show definition as the baseline
The rate is shown for the groups with a new rule and for regulars side by side
Booked appointments per week and regulars' rebooking are within 5% of baseline, or flagged
A verdict needs at least 100 booked appointments in the period, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close the comparison, record which change moved the no-show rate and what it cost, propose rules with their scope and plan the next round, including a refill list.

checks.name: The registered comparison is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this salon or any salon

hypotheses.statement: No-shows concentrate in new or first-time clients.
hypotheses.test: No-show rate for new clients against returning clients.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The new-client rate is at least 2 times the returning rate, with at least 30 new-client appointments.
hypotheses.refute_if: The rates are within 20% of each other.

hypotheses.statement: Appointments booked far ahead no-show more.
hypotheses.test: No-show rate by lead time (same week, 1 to 2 weeks, over 2 weeks).
hypotheses.confirm_if: The longest lead-time group has at least 1.5 times the shortest group's rate, with at least 30 appointments each.
hypotheses.refute_if: Rates are within 20% across lead times.

hypotheses.statement: Certain days or times have far more no-shows.
hypotheses.test: No-show rate by weekday and time of day.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A day or time block with at least 30 appointments has 1.5 times the average rate.
hypotheses.refute_if: All blocks are within 20% of the average.

hypotheses.statement: Certain services (long or high-value ones) no-show more or cost more when missed.
hypotheses.test: No-show rate and lost revenue by service.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A service with at least 30 bookings has 1.5 times the average rate or loses more than twice the average 45 pounds.
hypotheses.refute_if: Rates and losses are within 25% of the average across services.

hypotheses.statement: A single 24-hour reminder is not reaching or moving clients.
hypotheses.test: Share of no-shows whose reminder was not delivered or who had no valid number, and the rate for clients who got the reminder.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 20% of no-shows had no delivered reminder, or the reminded group's rate is above 14%.
hypotheses.refute_if: Nearly all no-shows were reminded and the reminded rate is already low.

hypotheses.statement: Rates differ by stylist because of marking habits or client mix, not only behaviour.
hypotheses.test: No-show rate by stylist, with client mix and the time each no-show was marked.
hypotheses.confirm_if: One stylist's rate is over 1.5 times the others and the marking time or client mix explains it.

hypotheses.statement: Regular clients rarely no-show, so a fee for everyone would cost more than it saves.
hypotheses.test: No-show rate for clients with 3 or more visits in 12 months.

hypotheses.statement: More reminders alone cannot reach under 8%.
hypotheses.test: Apply about a quarter fewer no-shows from the review to the baseline of 18%, then compare with 8%.
hypotheses.confirm_if: 18% less a quarter is about 13.5%, so more than half of the gap to 8% would remain.
hypotheses.refute_if: The reminded group's observed rate after the first step is already under 10%.

dropped.reason: Overbooking would make regular clients wait or turn them away, which the owner ruled out; a refill list is considered in the learning stage instead.

measurement.window: Weekly for the two months after the first setting change, against the 3-month baseline and the regulars as the unaffected group.
measurement.min_volume: At least 100 booked appointments in the period for an overall verdict, and at least 30 in a group for a group finding.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause a new fee rule if total weekly bookings fall more than 5% below baseline for two weeks in a row or regular clients complain about it; otherwise run the full window before a verdict.
